advices.diagnosis: The class exhibits a critical lack of cohesion (LCOM4=5) by mixing four distinct responsibilities: order lifecycle management, pricing logic, audit logging, and notification handling. This results in a high Weighted Method Count (WMC=56) and a high Number of Methods (NOM=26). The class acts as a 'God Object' that aggregates state and behavior for unrelated domains, making it difficult to test, maintain, and reuse. The high LCOM4 indicates that methods are not working together on a common set of attributes, confirming the presence of multiple independent sub-objects within a single class.

suggestions.title: Extract Pricing Logic into PricingService
suggestions.sketch: Move methods `set_discount`, `discount_for`, `bulk_discount`, `set_tax_rate`, `apply_tax`, `total_for`, `policy_rate`, and `is_priced` along with attributes `_tax_rate` and `_discounts` into a new `PricingService` class. `OrderService` should delegate pricing calculations to this new service. This removes the pricing component from the method-attribute graph, reducing LCOM4 and lowering the complexity and method count of `OrderService`.

suggestions.title: Extract Audit Logging into AuditLog
suggestions.sketch: Move methods `log`, `history`, `last_entry`, `audit_size`, and `clear_audit` along with attribute `_audit` into a new `AuditLog` class. `OrderService` should hold a reference to `AuditLog` and delegate audit operations. This isolates the audit component, further reducing LCOM4 and simplifying the `OrderService` interface.

suggestions.title: Extract Notification Handling into NotificationService
suggestions.sketch: Move methods `notify`, `sent_count`, and `reset_sent` along with attributes `_notifier` and `_sent` into a new `NotificationService` class. `OrderService` should delegate notification tasks to this service. This removes the notification component from the method-attribute graph, contributing to a lower LCOM4 and a more focused `OrderService`.

advices.risk_notes: Refactoring will increase the number of classes in the project and may increase the Dependency Count (DCC) of `OrderService` if it now depends on the new services. However, this is a trade-off for improved cohesion and maintainability. The `OrderService` will become a facade or orchestrator, which is a common and acceptable pattern. Tests will need to be updated to mock the new services. The `DAM` (Data Abstraction Metric) of `OrderService` may change depending on how the new services are injected, but the primary benefit is the reduction in LCOM4 and WMC.
